title: Day 723 — South Korea's Lee Jae-myung Makes First State Visit in 16 Years; Mexico and Korea Sign 17 Cooperation Agreements
detail: President Sheinbaum received South Korean President Lee Jae-myung at Palacio Nacional on September 24, 2026 (Day 723, Thursday), the first official visit by a South Korean head of state to Mexico since 2010. The two governments adopted the Plan de Acción México-Corea 2026-2030 and signed 17 memorandums of understanding spanning economic and financial cooperation, academic mobility, culture, tourism, science and technology, intellectual property, agriculture and security, including a plan for a K-pop culture center in Mexico and a Mexican cultural institute in South Korea. The countries also concluded a bilateral investment-promotion and protection agreement negotiated over seven years, and floated a $100 million credit scheme to help Mexican firms buy Korean goods and services. Officials cited $27 billion in 2025 bilateral trade and more than $11.5 billion in accumulated South Korean investment since 2006 across roughly 2,000 companies, with new cooperation areas flagged in artificial intelligence, aerospace, electromobility and supply chains; Sheinbaum's government also raised sharing intelligence databases and strategies against organized crime. Lee Jae-myung called Mexico "the tenth economic power and center of the global supply chain, a strategically relevant partner for Korea," while Sheinbaum said the two agreed on "deepening complementary economic cooperation that generates shared prosperity." Lee also signed the Senate's honor book during the visit.

media.caption: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung meets Claudia Sheinbaum at Palacio Nacional, the first South Korean state visit to Mexico in 16 years

title: Day 723 — LEGO to Invest $400 Million in Nuevo León Plant, 1,300 Jobs; Sheinbaum Clarifies Digital Economy Law Won't Ban Cash
detail: At her September 24, 2026 (Day 723) mañanera, Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard announced LEGO will invest $400 million (roughly 8.6 billion pesos) through 2029 to expand its Ciénaga de Flores, Nuevo León plant — already the company's largest in the world — adding about 62,000 square meters of industrial and automated-warehouse space and creating an estimated 1,300 jobs; formal groundbreaking is set for September 30, 2026. Ebrard cited the project as further evidence of rising foreign direct investment under the Plan México nearshoring strategy. Separately, Sheinbaum clarified that the government's proposed Digital Economy Law will not prohibit cash, but is meant to "facilitate the use of technology for digital payments," deepen financial inclusion and formalization, and build on existing tools like CoDi, according to the head of the Digital Transformation and Telecommunications Agency. Sheinbaum also ruled out cabinet changes, confirmed a Stray Kids concert is being arranged with 10 DIF-gifted tickets for low-income children, and said the U.S. would need Foreign Ministry (SRE) authorization to contract firms that notify deported Mexicans of immigration fines.

media.caption: Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard announces LEGO's $400 million Nuevo León expansion at Sheinbaum's September 24 mañanera
